en.title: Counting Three-Color Grid Colorings (Intuit OA)
en.description: Color an n×3 grid with three colors: red, green, and blue. A valid coloring requires every row and every column to contain at least two colors. The source's sample outputs for n=3 and n=4 contradict the statement; following the statement, they are corrected to 9750 and 296490 respectively. See the editorial for the derivation.
en.input: A single integer n (site range 1≤n≤10^18; the source gives no constraint on n).
en.output: Output the number of valid colorings modulo 1,000,000,007.
en.explanation: Apply inclusion-exclusion to the events that each of the three columns is entirely one color; the answer is 24^n−9·8^n+9·2^n+18·3^n−24 (modulo).
hints: Apply inclusion-exclusion to the three events "some column is entirely one color".
